explanation: Bin Jawad's § Aftermath makes the claim in its own words: "The Battle of Bin Jawad marked the end of the initial rebel offensive. Proving to be the high-water mark of the rebel offensive, it marked the end of the rebel advance westward at the time, and opened the way for a government counter-offensive that took pro-Gaddafi forces as far as the gates of Benghazi, before being pushed back by UN intervention." The counter-offensive reaching those gates is the second battle of Benghazi of 19 March. `enabled` and not `caused`: "opened the way for" is what the article says, and a counter-offensive has its own reasons. Probable: Wikipedia alone.
